title: Compose for Production
subtitle: Health checks, restart policies, secrets, resource limits, and production-ready patterns

content.text: Health checks — knowing your services are actually ready

content.code:
services:
  api:
    image: myapi
    healthcheck:
      # Command to run inside the container
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:3000/health"]
      # How often to check
      interval: 30s
      # How long to wait for a response
      timeout: 10s
      # How many failures before marking unhealthy
      retries: 3
      # Grace period before first check (startup time)
      start_period: 40s

  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3

content.filename: Secrets — never put passwords in environment
content.code:
# Production approach: use Docker secrets or env_file with .env

# Option 1: env_file (for simple setups)
services:
  api:
    image: myapi
    env_file:
      - .env.production   # file excluded from git

# Option 2: Docker secrets (Swarm/compose secrets)
secrets:
  db_password:
    file: ./secrets/db_password.txt  # or 'external: true' for Swarm
  jwt_secret:
    file: ./secrets/jwt_secret.txt

services:
  api:
    image: myapi
    secrets:
      - db_password
      - jwt_secret
    # Secrets mounted at /run/secrets/<name> — read them in your app

  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    secrets:
      - db_password
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/db_password

services:
  api:
    image: myapi
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '1.0'       # max 1 CPU core
          memory: 512M      # max 512 MB RAM
        reservations:
          cpus: '0.25'      # guaranteed minimum
          memory: 128M

  # Profiles — only start certain services in specific scenarios
  # docker compose --profile debug up
  debug-ui:
    image: adminer
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    profiles:
      - debug

  # docker compose --profile monitoring up
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus
    profiles:
      - monitoring

services:
  api:
    image: ghcr.io/myorg/api:${IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file: .env.production
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:3000/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512M
          cpus: '1.0'
    logging:
      driver: json-file
      options:
        max-size: "10m"
        max-file: "3"   # rotate: keep only 3 × 10 MB log files

  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file: .env.production
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $POSTGRES_USER"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1G

volumes:
  postgres-data:
    external: true   # must be created before compose up

questions.question: A service has 'depends_on: postgres: condition: service_healthy'. What does this require to work correctly?
options: postgres must have a 'healthcheck' defined — otherwise service_healthy is never true and your service never starts
the api service must also have a healthcheck
questions.explanation: condition: service_healthy waits until the dependency's healthcheck passes. If no healthcheck is defined on the dependency, it's never considered 'healthy' and your service hangs forever. Always define a healthcheck on any service you depend on with condition: service_healthy.

faq.q: Should I use Docker Compose in production?
faq.a: Yes, for single-server deployments — a small API, a personal project, or a startup's MVP. It's simple, well-understood, and reliable. For multi-server orchestration, automatic scaling, rolling deployments, or high availability, consider Kubernetes or managed container services (ECS, Cloud Run). Most projects run fine on a single server with Compose for years.

examples: IMAGE_TAG=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d — deploy a specific version by passing the SHA as an env var
Most indie SaaS products run their full stack on one $20/month VPS using Compose — nginx, API, postgres, redis — serving thousands of users reliably
